nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: 3 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (exact amount not specified but 3 mmol), 0.36 g urea, and 0.045 g NH4F were dissolved in 60 ml deionized water and stirred for 1 h to obtain a green solution. The solution was then transferred to a 100 ml Teflon-lined autoclave with pretreated carbon cloth (CC, 1.5 × 4 cm², pretreated with nitric acid and deionized water) as the growth substrate and heated at 180 °C for 24 h. Afterward, the CC was rinsed with deionized water and dried at 60 °C overnight.

nodes.name: Ru electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ru was electrochemically deposited onto the fabricated Ni(OH)2/CC in a three-electrode system, using Ni(OH)2/CC as the working electrode, a graphite rod as the counter electrode, and a saturated calomel electrode (SCE) as the reference electrode. The deposition was performed via linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) from -1.0 V to -1.5 V vs. SCE at a scan rate of 5 mV/s for 10 cycles in an electrolyte composed of 50 mL of 1 M KOH and 5 mg of RuCl3·xH2O. The resulting Ru/Ni(OH)2 was cleaned with deionized water and dried at 60 °C overnight.

nodes.name: Varying Ru content synthesis
nodes.procedure: Under the optimized annealing condition of 300 °C, a series of Ruy-Ni-300 catalysts with varying Ru content were synthesized by adjusting the amount of RuCl3·xH2O added during the preparation of Ru-Ni-300. Specifically, the initial Ru precursor amount of 5 mg was altered to 1 mg, 2.5 mg, and 10 mg, defining the Ru content ratio as y (y = 0.2, 0.5, and 2).

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation in 1.0 M KOH using three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: The alkaline HER activity of Ru-Ni-x catalysts, including Ru/Ni(OH)2, was evaluated by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte using a standard three-electrode setup. As illustrated in Fig. 2a and b, Ru/Ni(OH)2 displays suboptimal performance... However, the incorporation of NiO significantly enhances HER activity... Specifically, the Ru-Ni-300 sample... exhibits the best performance with η10 and η100 decreasing to 23 and 71 mV, respectively... the desired Ru-Ni-300 exhibiting the smallest Tafel slope (41 mV/dec)... Ru-Ni-300 exhibits the lowest resistance across all these processes (Table S2), particularly exhibiting a minimal intermediates adsorption/desorption resistance (0.69 Ω)... The mass activity of Ru-Ni-300 is approximately 1.5-fold and 3.6-fold higher... Long-term stability tests conducted at current densities of 10 and 100 mA/cm2 over 100 h (Fig. 2i) reveal remarkable retention.

nodes.description: Commercial Pt/C benchmark HER performance in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: To benchmark practical performance, Ru-Ni-300 was compared to commercial Pt/C (Fig. S5). At 10 mA/cm2, both catalysts show similar overpotentials 23 mV for Ru-Ni-300 vs. 22 mV for Pt/C). However, at 100 mA/cm2, Ru-Ni-300 outperforms Pt/C, requiring only 71 mV compared to 104 mV... surpassing that of Pt/C (44 mV/dec, Fig. S5b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/Ni(OH)₂ and Ru-Ni-250 show only Ni(OH)₂ phase (JCPDS No. 59-0462). Ru-Ni-300 shows coexistence of Ni(OH)₂ and NiO (JCPDS No. 47-1049). Ru-Ni-350 and Ru-Ni-400 show single NiO phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structures of the samples were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, as shown in Fig. 1b. The Ru/Ni(OH)₂ and Ru-Ni-250 samples exhibit only the Ni(OH)₂ phase (JCPDS No. 59-0462). ... When the temperature exceeds 350 °C, Ni(OH)₂ in the Ru-Ni-350 and Ru-Ni-400 samples fully converts into a single NiO phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/Ni(OH)₂ shows peaks at 454 and 3571 cm⁻¹ characteristic of Ni(OH)₂. Ru-Ni-400 shows peaks at 590, 707, and 1098 cm⁻¹ corresponding to NiO. Ru-Ni-300 shows peaks from both Ni(OH)₂ and NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy further validates these findings by revealing structure-specific vibrational modes (Fig. 1c). ... the Ru/Ni(OH)₂ sample exhibits prominent peaks at 454 and 3571 cm⁻¹, characteristic of Ni(OH)₂ [32,33]. Conversely, the Ru-Ni-400 sample displays peaks at 590, 707, and 1098 cm⁻¹, corresponding to NiO [34].

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni-300 shows vertically grown Ni-based nanosheets on carbon fibers of CC, nanosheet structure remains consistent after Ru deposition or annealing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The overall morphology and structure of these materials were examined via scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Fig. 1d and S1 reveal vertically grown Ni-based nanosheets on the carbon fibers of CC, and the nanosheet structure remains consistent after Ru deposition or annealing.

nodes.characterization_summary: Low-magnification TEM shows numerous Ru nanoparticles anchored onto Ni-based nanosheet support in all samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The low-magnification TEM shows numerous Ru nanoparticles (NPs) anchored onto the Ni-based nanosheet support in all samples (Fig. 1e and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni-300 shows coexistence of Ru NPs, Ni(OH)₂, and NiO with lattice spacings of 2.16 Å (002) for Ru, 2.31 Å (101) for Ni(OH)₂, 2.09 Å (200) and 1.45 Å (220) for NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For the Ru-Ni-300 sample, HRTEM confirms the coexistence of Ru NPs, Ni(OH)₂, and NiO crystalline phases (Fig. 1f), as determined by the typical (002) planes of Ru, (101) of Ni(OH)₂, (200) and (220) planes of NiO, with corresponding lattice spacings of 2.16 Å, 2.31 Å, 2.09 Å, and 1.45 Å, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni-300 shows uniform distribution of Ru, Ni, and O elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping demonstrates the uniform distribution of Ru, Ni, and O elements throughout the Ru-Ni-300 sample (Fig. 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni-300 has Ru loading of 5.6 μg/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) analysis reveals a very low Ru loading of 5.6 μg/cm² in the Ru-Ni-300 sample (Table S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS of all catalysts shows three peaks for lattice oxygen (M-O), hydroxyl (OH), and adsorbed oxygen. Ru-Ni-300 exhibits lowest OH binding energy indicating strongest Lewis basicity of surface OH species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3a, the O 1s XPS spectra of the five samples can be deconvoluted into three distinct peaks, corresponding to lattice oxygen (M-O), hydroxyl group (OH), and adsorbed oxygen species [38,39]. A noticeable shift in the binding energy of OH groups is observed across the series, following a volcano-type trend. Ru-Ni-300 is positioned at the volcano peak, displaying the lowest OH binding energy

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows OH stretching modes at 3230 cm⁻¹ (4HB-H₂O), 3424 cm⁻¹ (2HB-H₂O), 3580 cm⁻¹ (Ni(OH)₂). Ru-Ni-300 exhibits highest Stark slopes and Ni-OH peak at 521 cm⁻¹ vanishes at lower overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman spectra of (c) Ru-Ni-300, (d) Ru-Ni-400, and (e) Ru/Ni(OH)₂ catalysts. ... a broad band observed in the 3200-3800 cm⁻¹ region corresponds to the OH stretching mode. Through Gaussian fitting, it can be deconvoluted into three distinct peaks at 3230, 3424, and 3580 cm⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s quasi-in-situ XPS during HER shows Ru-Ni-300 maintains constant OH/(OH+M-O) proportion while Ru/Ni(OH)₂ and Ru-Ni-400 show increasing OH content with overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quasi-in-situ O 1s XPS spectra are displayed in Fig. 4a–c. By quantifying the relative content of OH species at different overpotentials ... For Ru/Ni(OH)₂ and Ru-Ni-400 catalysts, their OH contents gradually increase with higher overpotentials ... Conversely, for the Ru-Ni-300 sample, the surface OH content remained relatively constant

properties.data_points: Increasing trend from low to high overpotential

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA-normalized CV shows Ru-Ni-300 has smallest OH adsorption peak area (0.3-0.9 V) indicating best OH tolerance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To better understand the OH adsorption/desorption behavior on the surface, we conducted cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements. ... the Ru/Ni(OH)₂ catalyst exhibited the largest OH adsorption peak area within the potential range of 0.3-0.9 V, whereas Ru-Ni-300 showed the smallest peak area.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Ni-300 exhibits lowest isoelectric point (IEP) among samples, consistent with strongest OH Lewis basicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further support the OH Lewis basicity hypothesis, we performed isoelectric point (IEP) measurements (Fig. S13). ... Ru-Ni-300 exhibits the lowest IEP among the samples, consistent with its strongest Lewis basicity inferred from XPS.
